SkiaSharp's SKVertices.CreateCopy takes only exact-length managed arrays and copies them into native memory, so a mesh shading makes a position array, and a texture array for a textured mesh, that cannot come from a pool. Once per mesh while a page is recorded.
ArrayPool<byte>.Shared makes the table of idle arrays for a size class the first time that class is rented, once per process and size class.
The first shading paint builds its colour function tables and resource caches. This happens once per page recording; warm tiles replay the picture.
The first image use grows the image cache's entry array. This happens once per page recording; warm tiles replay the picture.
A path builder grows its command array as the content stream adds segments. This happens once per path built while the page is recorded; warm tiles replay the picture.
Each path builder owns a command list. Builders are created while the page is recorded; warm tiles replay the picture.

ColdOpenAndRender opens a new document on every operation, so the page's first sh operator parses the shading once and adds it to that document's shading cache. The JIT inlined the cache insert into OpPaintShading. WarmReplay replays the recorded picture and does not repeat it.

Saving as PDF/A runs the content once to learn which codes each non-embedded font shows; the set of codes per font grows as text is shown. The JIT inlined the device's set insert into ShowCode. Conversion is a user action.
Saving as PDF/A records the codes shown by font; the map from font to codes grows once per font. The JIT inlined the device's map insert into ShowCode. Conversion is a user action.
Saving as PDF/A creates one code record for each font its content shows. The JIT inlined the device's insert into ShowCode. Conversion is a user action.
Saving as PDF/A edits a private copy of the document: adding the metadata stream, output intent profile and embedded font objects grows the copy's edit table. The copy is discarded after the save.
Saving as PDF/A edits a private copy of the document: replacing the catalog and fixed objects grows the copy's edit table. The copy is discarded after the save.
Saving as PDF/A reads the old XMP dates to carry them into the new packet; each date read returns its text before it is parsed. Conversion is a user action.
Validating a document's signatures builds one report, byte range check and change list per signature. It runs once when a caller asks for the signatures to be checked, never while rendering.
Validation loads the document security store's certificates into one collection, shared by every signature of the document; once per validation.

Checking a signature reads its signed bytes into one array, because SignedCms takes detached content as an array, and decodes the container with SignedCms, whose ASN.1 model, certificates, OIDs and attribute objects (read for the message digest, signing time and timestamp) are allocated by System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs. Measured at about 20 KB per SHA-256, SHA3-256 or SHAKE256 signature including the chain; it runs once per signature when a caller validates.
Building the signer's chain uses X509Chain, which allocates its policy, stores, native handles and chain elements. Once per signature or timestamp when a caller validates.

SHA-1, SHA-2 and SHA-3 signers are checked with SignerInfo.CheckSignature, which re-encodes the signed attributes and creates a hash provider and the certificate's public key. Once per signature when signatures are validated.

A SHAKE256 signer is checked by hashing with stack and pooled buffers; the allocations are the certificate's public key object (its ECDsa or RSA wrapper, native key handle, parsed extensions and PublicKey), which .NET creates on each GetECDsaPublicKey or GetRSAPublicKey call. Once per signature when signatures are validated.

Decrypting an AES-GCM string or stream returns one array sized to the plain text, which the caller owns. The array is cleared by the platform when authentication fails. It runs when a string is parsed or a stream is decoded, not during rendering of decoded data.
Saving an encrypted document returns one array per encrypted string or stream holding the IV, cipher text and tag. Saving is a user action.
The AES-GCM instance is created once per security handler, on the first AES-GCM string or stream, and reused for every object.
The AES-GCM instance is created once per security handler, on the first AES-GCM string or stream, and reused for every object. The trace attributes it here when the creation is inlined.
Opening a revision 7 file checks /Perms once with a short-lived AES instance, which the .NET cipher backs with a native cipher context.

The revision 6 and 7 password hash (ISO 32000-2 algorithm 2.B) runs its AES-128 rounds on the CPU's AES instructions and allocates nothing. Only a CPU without them uses the .NET cipher, which backs each new key with a native cipher context and key box. It runs once per open or save that checks a password.

Writing a new standard security handler dictionary returns the values it stores: the file key, the owner and user strings, the wrapped keys and the permissions block. The saved file's encryption keeps these arrays. It runs once per save that encrypts, which is a user action.
The /Encrypt dictionary and its crypt filter dictionaries are new objects made at their final size. The save keeps them to write the file. It runs once per save that encrypts, which is a user action.

A save that encrypts makes one plan: the security handler that encrypts every object, the encryption dictionary and the file id dictionary. It runs once per save that encrypts, which is a user action.
Describing a document's protection returns one record to the caller. It runs when a protection check or change asks, which is a user action.

Deriving the file key returns the key as a new array that the security handler keeps. The hash input is gathered in a pooled buffer and hashed in one call. It runs once per open or save of a public-key file.
The first time the program creates a cipher or hash type, the runtime builds that type's activator cache once for the life of the process.
The first time the program creates a cipher or hash type, the runtime builds that type's activator cache once for the life of the process.

Signing writes one update per signature. It opens an edit that records the objects it changes (the transaction and its sets and lists of changed object numbers and states) and returns the signed file. It runs once per signature, which is a user action.

Planning a signature makes the plan and plan result records and reads the signer's name from the certificate. The message arrays exist only when there is a reason or note to report. It runs once per signature, and the signature keeps the plan until the file is finished.
Building a signature makes the prepared file record, the digest of the signed bytes and the result record that holds the signed file. It runs once per signature, which is a user action.
The prepared file is one object that remembers where the signature value goes. It runs once per signature, which is a user action.

A signature adds its objects to the document: the signature field and widget, the appearance, and copies of the catalog, interactive form and annotation list that the update changes. These objects are the content of the update. It runs once per signature, which is a user action.

The signature dictionary is a new document object. It holds the byte range array and the name, date, reason and location strings, and a reference dictionary only for a certification or a lock. It runs once per signature, which is a user action.
The description of the signature for screen readers is encoded into the one byte array the field stores. It runs once per visible or new signature field, which is a user action.

The .NET returns a new private key object each time a key is asked for, so the caller can dispose it, and the signer cannot keep one without becoming disposable. Each signature creates and disposes one.
A hash object holds a native context. It is created the first time a digest is used and the next signature reuses it through a one-slot pool, so this runs once per digest for the life of the process.

Reading the finished file back to check it opens the file as a document, with its object store, caches and locks, and validates the new signature. It runs once per signature unless the options turn VerifyOutput off.
The signed attributes are returned as one array that the caller signs and keeps. They are written with a pooled DER writer. It runs once per signature.
The signature container is returned as one array that is written into the reserved room. It is written with a pooled DER writer. It runs once per signature.
Adding validation data builds the update: its edit, the result record and the notes. It runs once per call, which is a user action.

Adding validation data creates one stream for each new certificate, response or list, and the arrays and dictionaries of the document security store. These objects are the content of the update. It runs once per call, which is a user action.

A document with an interactive form has its fields walked to find a free field name or the field to sign. The walk makes each field's name and a record for each signature field. It runs once per signature, and only when the document has a form.
The first time the program creates a key, certificate or hash type, the runtime builds that type's activator cache once for the life of the process.
The first time the program creates a key, certificate or hash type, the runtime builds that type's activator cache once for the life of the process.
The details of a document's signature fields are read once and cached on the document: one record per field with the signer name, location and contact text, and the array that holds them.
A field's full name is written straight into the one string it returns. The signature details and the field walks keep it. It runs once per signature field read.

The file key of an RC4 or AES-128 file is 5 to 16 bytes, returned as an array because the encryption writer keeps it for the file. Hashing its input uses the stack. Once per file written with these handlers.

The file key (5 to 16 bytes) that a correct password gives is copied out of the stack buffer into an array, because the handler keeps it for the life of the document. Once per open of an RC4 or AES-128 file.
Unwrapping the file key from /UE or /OE creates one AES instance once per open.
Each security handler owns one AES instance and one lock, created when the document opens and reused for every object.

Combining /Info with the XMP packet joins several creators into one author string and holds the chosen title, subject and keyword strings for the returned information record. The properties dialog reads this once per document.
The combined information is a new record built with a copy of the /Info record, which the caller keeps. The properties dialog reads it once per document.

Reading a portfolio builds the records the caller keeps: schema fields, sort keys, the folder tree with its free ranges, and each file's collection values as strings. This runs once when a portfolio is opened, not while pages render.

A declaration that is not in the catalog yet copies the catalog and its /Extensions dictionary and builds the new extension dictionary and its array, which the catalog keeps. A declaration the catalog already holds is found by comparing, and allocates nothing.
The JSON writer grows its buffer as the debug view is written to the stream, and a stream's Base64 text is built once. The view is a debugging aid, not a render path.
Content normalisation adds one image per moved inline image and one stream per changed page. The bytes are the new object's data, which the document keeps in its edit layer until it is saved.

Saving as PDF 2.0 opens one private working copy of the file, so the fixes never touch the open document. The copy reads the cross-reference data again into its own object slot arrays, name table and caches. It runs once per copy, a user action.
The working copy replays the open document's unsaved edits, so the copy lists the edited objects once. It runs once per copy, a user action.

A PDF 2.0 copy creates its session with the note lists, the result and the note arrays it returns, the bytes of the written file, and one extra read of that file to check its header, page count and document information. It runs once per copy, a user action.

Moving the document information into XMP builds one plan: the XMP changes, the names of the moved entries, the sentences for values left out, and the copy of the information dictionary. The notes are strings the user reads. It runs once per copy.
Comparing the XMP value an information entry maps to joins the creators and keywords into one string per entry that the XMP holds. It runs once per copy.
Matching the two dates to the XMP formats a PDF date and a note sentence when they differ. It runs once per copy.
Reading a document information value as text creates its string once per entry. It runs once per copy.
Writing the XMP creates the packet bytes, the metadata stream dictionary and the copy of the catalog that points at them. It runs once per copy.

Writing the F operator as f collects the content stream objects into one set, then decodes each stream that is rewritten, copies it, and compresses it again. A stream with no F operator is not copied. It runs once per copy.
The dictionary pass collects the reachable objects once and holds its counts in one tally. A dictionary is copied only when a deprecated entry is removed. It runs once per copy.
The summary builds one note, with its sentence, for each kind of change or refusal found. It runs once per copy.

Removing operating system file names copies the file specification dictionary, as the open document's dictionary is never changed. A dictionary with none of those entries is not copied. It runs once per copy.
Removing deprecated catalog entries copies the catalog, and each nested dictionary it changes, once. It runs once per copy.
Setting the version removes the catalog's /Version through a copy of the catalog, and records one note for the header and one for the file identifier. It runs once per copy.
Drawing form field appearances reads the form's widgets into lists, and records one note per kind of change. It runs once per copy, and only for a form.

Decrypting an AES-CBC string or stream sets the key on the handler's AES instance, which .NET copies into a native key box, and runs the cipher through native contexts. It runs when an encrypted string is parsed or a stream is decoded, not while a decoded page is drawn.

Saving an encrypted document encrypts each string and stream with AES-CBC: the handler sets the key on its AES instance, which .NET copies into a native key box, and runs the cipher through native contexts. Saving is a user action.
A save takes one snapshot of the edited objects, a sorted array and its object numbers. It runs once per save.

Checking a PDF MAC token (ISO/TS 32004) keys an AES cipher to unwrap the MAC key and an HMAC to check the attributes, and .NET backs both with native contexts, key boxes and provider objects; the OID read from the token for the digest is a string. It runs once per revision when the document is checked, not while rendering.

Checking a standalone PDF MAC reads the four byte range numbers and the token into small arrays the check keeps for its length, hashes the covered bytes with an incremental hash that .NET backs with native contexts, and returns one result record. It runs once per revision when the document is checked.

Checking a PDF MAC attached to a signature reads the byte range numbers into an array, hashes the covered bytes and the signature value with an incremental hash that .NET backs with native contexts, and returns one result record. It runs once per signed revision when the document is checked.

Checking a document's PDF MAC opens each revision's structure without decrypting it (a prefix view of the file, an object store with its name table, cross-reference table and caches), reads that revision's own trailer, and returns one result per revision and one report. It runs once per document, when the report is first asked for, and the report is cached.

Reading the permissions the encrypted /Perms entry protects uses a short-lived AES instance, which .NET backs with a native cipher context. It runs once per document when the report is first asked for.
Deriving the key-encryption key runs HKDF with HMAC-SHA-256, which .NET backs with native hash contexts. It runs once per token.
Hashing the covered bytes of a PDF MAC uses an incremental hash that .NET backs with native contexts. It runs once per token.

Listing a file's revisions follows the cross-reference chain once, building the list of section offsets and the revision array, and the document caches the result. It runs when signatures or the PDF MAC are checked.

Writing a PDF MAC token builds its DER with ASN.1 writers, derives and wraps the MAC key with .NET cryptography objects, and returns the token array. It runs once per saved revision of an encrypted document that requires a PDF MAC.
Attaching a PDF MAC token to a signature copies the signature container through ASN.1 reader and writer objects and returns the new container. It runs once per signed revision that is written.

Sealing a saved revision with a PDF MAC builds the /AuthCode dictionary and its byte range array, writes the trailer section more than once while the byte range settles, and hashes the covered bytes with an incremental hash that .NET backs with native contexts. It runs once per saved revision of an encrypted document that requires a PDF MAC.

A thread that waits for another thread's decode of the same image blocks on a monitor, and the runtime makes that thread's wait handle the first time it does. Once per thread that ever waits.
A thread that waits for another thread's decode of the same image blocks on a monitor, and the runtime makes that thread's wait handle the first time it does. Once per thread that ever waits.
A pool makes its table of 12 kept-array slots when the first large array is returned to it. Once per element type for each scratch owner.
A scratch owner makes its lock and one small pool object for each element type it rents, on first use. A document owns one owner; a standalone decode that is given none makes its own. Once per owner.
A scratch owner makes its lock and one small pool object for each element type it rents, on first use. A document owns one owner; a standalone decode that is given none makes its own. Once per owner.

A document with a damaged structure logs the repair, such as a rebuilt cross-reference table, in the open context's log. The viewer tells the user what was repaired. Once per damaged document; a clean document logs nothing.

A document with a damaged structure logs the repair, such as a rebuilt cross-reference table, in the open context's log. The viewer tells the user what was repaired. Once per damaged document; a clean document logs nothing.
The object-slot array of a document is made once per open, sized to the cross-reference table. It is cleared and reused after the /Root check and after authentication when the size is unchanged.
Opening a document from a byte array wraps the array in the document's byte source. One per opened document.
The transaction object is the handle callers use to commit or roll back an edit. One per edit.

The cache of generated annotation appearances is made when a document first draws an annotation that has no appearance: the cache object, its lock and its map. Once per document and render settings; documents without such annotations never make it.

The cache of generated annotation appearances is made when a document first draws an annotation that has no appearance: the cache object, its lock and its map. Once per document and render settings; documents without such annotations never make it.

The cache of generated annotation appearances is made when a document first draws an annotation that has no appearance: the cache object, its lock and its map. Once per document and render settings; documents without such annotations never make it.

The cache of generated annotation appearances is made when a document first draws an annotation that has no appearance: the cache object, its lock and its map. Once per document and render settings; documents without such annotations never make it.

The cache of generated annotation appearances is made when a document first draws an annotation that has no appearance: the cache object, its lock and its map. Once per document and render settings; documents without such annotations never make it.

The cache of generated annotation appearances is made when a document first draws an annotation that has no appearance: the cache object, its lock and its map. Once per document and render settings; documents without such annotations never make it.
A renderer makes the list that holds its recent page pictures, sized for its 32 page limit. Once per renderer.
A renderer makes the list that holds its recent page pictures, sized for its 32 page limit. Once per renderer.

A renderer finds the document's shared render cache for its image and drawing settings. The first renderer of a document with a given set of settings creates the cache, its entry and the table that holds them; later renderers with the same settings find them.

An interpreter is made only when none is idle, once for each thread that records at the same time, and is then reused with its state stacks and path builders for every page, pattern cell and soft mask.

A recording device is made only when none is idle, once for each thread that records at the same time, with its picture recorder, builders, paints, lists and glyph cache; it is then reused. A knockout group inside a recording makes its own picture recorder for the group.
A recording device makes its image counter once and reuses it for every recording.
The object that tracks a paused page recording is made only when none is idle and is then reused.
The slots that keep each kind of idle object (interpreters, devices, recordings, decoders) are made once per process on first use.
The clip path of a page size is made the first time that size is recorded and then shared by every page of the same size.
A zlib or deflate decoder is made only when none is idle and is returned after each decode; at most four of each are kept for all documents.
Recording annotation appearances makes the annotation pass object that holds the page being drawn. Once per annotation recording; the picture is cached with the page.

Records a page's annotation appearances into a picture the first time a zoom band or print mode needs them: the annotation pass, the appearance forms and the native wrappers of the result. The picture is cached with the page, so warm tiles replay it.

A drawn mark is the result the signature pad keeps: the record, its point array and its stroke length array. The smoothed points it is made from are on the stack or in a pooled array. Once per finished stroke.
The page entries are the result of reading the page tree, in one array sized from the root /Count and kept by the page set, once per read of the page tree.
The table of distinct attributes that pages inherit is kept by the page set, with four entries to start. Once per read of the page tree.
Opening with options makes the open context that carries the token, the recovery switches and the repair log, once per open.
Reading the cross-reference structure makes the lock that guards loading object streams, once per open.
The first object read from an object stream makes the cache of decoded streams and its lock, once per document that has object streams.
The first object read from an object stream makes the cache of decoded streams, once per document that has object streams.
A thread that waits on the store's lock while another thread parses makes the runtime's wait object once; the runtime owns it.
The first edit of a document makes the table of edited objects and its key array, once per document that is edited.
A document opened without drawing services makes empty ones the first time it needs them, once per document.
The first name that the library does not know makes the document's lookup of added names, its lock and its tables, once per document; known names never reach it.
The repairs are returned as a copy, so the caller can keep them while the document goes on reporting. One array per call.
The decoded hint table is the bytes the hint reader parses, once per hint stream read.

The page set is the result of reading the page tree: it keeps the entry array and the attribute table that the reader built, and every reader of the document shares it. Once per read of the page tree.

ColdOpenAndRender opens a new document on every operation, and the document's page set makes its table of made pages (inlined into the benchmark method) with the first page it hands out, once per open.

The cache factory in GetPaint makes the paint for a pattern at a placement the first time it is selected; the render cache then shares it, so a page that selects the same pattern again allocates nothing. The cold benchmark opens a new document, with a new cache, on every operation.
Queuing helper work to the thread pool (inlined into LoadStrip) makes the runtime grow its own queue segments now and then; the pool owns them and a strip makes none when the pool already has room.

Queuing helper work to the thread pool makes the runtime grow the local work queue of a thread, and a new pool thread makes its thread-static storage; the runtime owns both and they happen once per thread.
Queuing helper work to the thread pool makes the runtime add a segment to its global queue when the current one is full; the pool owns it and reuses the queue.

A thread that blocks on a monitor for the first time makes the runtime's wait object for itself. The caller blocks only when a helper is still inside the loop after the caller has done its share, so this happens once per thread that ever waits.
The runtime makes the wait handle behind a monitor the first time a thread blocks on it, once per thread that ever waits for a helper.
The runtime makes the event behind a monitor the first time a thread blocks on it, once per thread that ever waits for a helper.
The decoded image is the result of the decode; its pixels are rented and the record that carries them to the caller is made once per decoded image.
The first rent of a type on a thread makes that thread's table in the shared array pool; the runtime owns it and a thread makes it once.

The first read of a certificate's DER bytes makes the certificate export them (inlined into Check). SignedCms makes a new certificate object for each signature it decodes, so the export happens once per validated signature; the bytes are then parsed in place.
The shared array pool makes a content buffer when its bucket is empty, as on a new render thread or after it trimmed itself under memory pressure; a warm thread reuses its buffer.
The first code on a new render thread to touch some thread-static state makes that thread's static storage array; the runtime owns it and a thread makes it once.
A document makes its renderer with its first render and keeps it until an edit replaces it, so its caches and recorded pages are reused. Once per document.
The options record carries the form highlight colour into the document's renderer, which keeps it; it is made with that renderer, once per document.
A document's font cache keeps its first font in inline fields and makes its map only when a second distinct font is used, so later lookups are by key. Once per document that uses two or more fonts.
A document's pattern-cell cache keeps its first cell in inline fields and makes its map only when a second distinct pattern is used. Once per document that uses two or more patterns.
The entry array of that pattern-cell map, sized for its first keys. Once per document that uses two or more patterns.
A document's shading cache keeps its first shading in inline fields and makes its map only when a second distinct shading is used. Once per document that uses two or more shadings.
The entry array of that shading map, sized for its first keys. Once per document that uses two or more shadings.

The record of one image decode in progress, made by the thread that decodes an image that is not cached, so a second thread waits for it instead of decoding again. Once per decoded image, next to the decode itself; never for a cached image or when a recorded tile is drawn.
The table of decodes in progress makes its entry array when the first decode of a document starts. Once per document.

The pixel array of a decoded image is the decode result: the image cache keeps it (up to 64 MiB) and the recorded page draws from it, so it cannot be pooled. It is zeroed because a truncated image keeps the rows it did not receive as transparent black. Once per image while it stays cached; never when a recorded tile is drawn.

A document whose drawing services do not share decoder buffers makes its own scratch owner the first time one of its streams is decoded. The owner keeps the document reusable decoder buffers and is released with the document. Once per document.
XmlReader reads from a Stream, so each XMP packet is wrapped in a 56-byte read-only view of its bytes without copying them. Once per XMP packet parsed, which is once per document for its metadata.
The first read of a compressed object, the trailer Root, makes the document cache of decoded object streams. Once per document that has object streams.
The lock of the document cache of decoded object streams, made with the cache when the first compressed object is read. Once per document that has object streams.
The first time a thread returns an array to the runtime's shared array pool, the pool makes that thread's own bucket table. The runtime owns it and each decode worker thread makes it once.
The runtime's per-thread table of the shared array pool is registered in a conditional table, which grows once per new decode worker thread.
The container of that conditional table is replaced once per new decode worker thread.
The runtime's per-thread table of the shared array pool is registered in a conditional table, which grows once per new decode worker thread.
The container of that conditional table is replaced once per new decode worker thread.
The runtime's per-thread table of the shared array pool keeps its entries in an object array that is made once per new decode worker thread.
